newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bank shares tumble further on profit taking.
newsitem.headline: Canada bank shares tumble further on profit taking.

text.p: Shares in Canada's big banks sank on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Wednesday as investors continued to grab profits from the high-flying bank group.
The TSE's financial services sector was down 133 points, or 2.5 percent, in brisk midday trading.

The group lost 3.4 percent on Tuesday after a Canadian brokerage house lowered its recommendations on four of the so-called big six banks. "It's more of a profit-taking stall as opposed to the end of the (rally)," a banking analyst said.
Bank stocks have soared to all-time highs in recent months, with Toronto's bank index up 46 percent in 1996.
Royal Bank of Canada, the country's biggest bank, led the slide in financial services. The shares were off 1.80 at 44.20 at midday in heavy turnover of 1.1 million shares.
Toronto-Dominion Bank fell 1.50 to 31.90 on 996,000 shares, followed by Bank of Montreal, down 1.50 to 40.65 on 858,000 shares.
Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce shed 1.45 to 55.80 on 508,000 shares. Bank of Nova Scotia dropped 1.35 to 43.15 on 740,000 shares.
National Bank of Canada, the smallest of the big six, eased 0.20 to 13.15 on 545,000 shares.
The analyst said several factors suggest bank stocks will resume their climb, including a strong Canadian dollar which is helping to stabilize domestic interest rates at their current low levels.
"The inflation scare which would end the party just isn't in the cards yet," the analyst said.

Other analysts have said the group was still popular among foreign investors seeking to jump into the Canadian market, lured by interest rates at 40-year lows and a recovering economy. -- Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8100 (c) Reuters Limited 1996
